rows.speaker: ابن عباس وابن مسعود وناس من الصحابة
rows.claim: They explain the bargain as taking misguidance and abandoning guidance.
rows.anchor: قال: أخذوا الضلالة وتركوا الهدى

rows.speaker: ابن عباس
rows.claim: Through Ibn Ishaq's route, the exchange means disbelief for faith.
rows.anchor: عن ابن عباس: {أولئك الذين اشتروا الضلالة بالهدى} أي: الكفر بالإيمان

rows.speaker: مجاهد
rows.claim: The hypocrites first believed and then disbelieved.
rows.anchor: وقال مجاهد: آمنوا ثم كفروا

rows.speaker: قتادة
rows.claim: They preferred misguidance over guidance, meaning disbelief over faith; Ibn Kathir compares this to Thamud's choice of blindness.
rows.anchor: وقال قتادة: استحبوا الضلالة على الهدى

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: The commentators' common point is that hypocrites exchanged guidance for error, whether they apostatized after belief or preferred error from the outset; they comprised different kinds.
rows.anchor: أن المنافقين عدلوا عن الهدى إلى الضلال، واعتاضوا عن الهدى بالضلالة

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Their deal yielded no profit: their transaction failed, and their conduct was not rightly guided.
rows.anchor: أي: ما ربحت صفقتهم في هذه البيعة، {وما كانوا مهتدين} أي: راشدين في صنيعهم ذلك

rows.speaker: قتادة
rows.claim: He describes them as moving from guidance to error, unity to division, security to fear, and Sunnah to innovation; Ibn Abi Hatim transmits the same report.
rows.anchor: خرجوا من الهدى إلى الضلالة، ومن الجماعة إلى الفرقة

rows.speaker: ابن عباس وابن مسعود وناس من الصحابة
rows.claim: When the hypocrites heard the fire and rainstorm parables, they objected that God was too exalted to use such examples; this occasioned the passage through 'the losers.'
rows.anchor: قال المنافقون: الله أعلى وأجل من أن يضرب هذه الأمثال

rows.speaker: قتادة
rows.claim: After God mentioned the spider and fly, the polytheists questioned why they were mentioned, and this verse was revealed.
rows.anchor: قال المشركون: ما بال العنكبوت والذباب يذكران؟

rows.speaker: قتادة
rows.claim: God does not refrain from stating the truth through anything, great or small; the objection to the fly and spider prompted the verse.
rows.anchor: حين ذكر في كتابه الذباب والعنكبوت قال أهل الضلالة: ما أراد الله من ذكر هذا؟

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: The first wording attributed to Qatada suggests a Meccan setting, which Ibn Kathir rejects; Qatada's second wording is more accurate, and Mujahid reports it similarly.
rows.anchor: العبارة الأولى عن قتادة فيها إشعار أن هذه الآية مكية، وليس كذلك

rows.speaker: الحسن وإسماعيل بن أبي خالد
rows.claim: Ibn Abi Hatim reports that both gave an account resembling those of al-Suddi and Qatada.
rows.anchor: روي عن الحسن وإسماعيل بن أبي خالد نحو قول السدي وقتادة

rows.speaker: الربيع بن أنس
rows.claim: He likens worldly abundance to a mosquito that dies once full: people in the parable are seized when they become satiated with worldly life; he cites 6:44. Ibn Abi Hatim gives a similar route, and Ibn Kathir leaves the matter to God.
rows.anchor: هذا مثل ضربه الله للدنيا؛ إذ البعوضة تحيا ما جاعت، فإذا سمنت ماتت

rows.speaker: ابن جرير
rows.claim: He chooses al-Suddi's occasion-of-revelation account because it best fits this surah; Ibn Kathir agrees that it is suitable.
rows.anchor: وقد اختار ابن جرير ما حكاه السدي؛ لأنه أمس بالسورة، وهو مناسب

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Here 'does not feel shy' means does not disdain or fear to give any sort of example, large or small.
rows.anchor: أي: لا يستنكف، وقيل: لا يخشى أن يضرب مثلا ما، أي: أي مثل كان

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: One grammatical account makes ما a minimizer and بعوضة an accusative appositive; another treats ما as an indefinite noun qualified by بعوضة.
rows.anchor: "ما" هاهنا للتقليل (2) وتكون {بعوضة} منصوبة على البدل

rows.speaker: ابن جرير
rows.claim: He treats ما as a relative pronoun and بعوضة as inflected like it; Arabic can inflect a relative-clause element like ما or من, which may be definite or indefinite.
rows.anchor: واختار ابن جرير أن ما موصولة، و {بعوضة} معربة بإعرابها

rows.speaker: حسان بن ثابت
rows.claim: Ibn Jarir cites Hassan's verse as linguistic evidence for inflecting the complement of ما or من in the same way as the pronoun.
rows.anchor: حب (6) النبي محمد إيانا (7)

rows.speaker: الكسائي والفراء
rows.claim: They allow an omitted preposition, understanding the wording as an example extending from a mosquito to what is above it.
rows.anchor: وتقدير الكلام: إن الله لا يستحيي أن يضرب مثلا ما بين بعوضة

rows.speaker: الضحاك وإبراهيم بن أبي عبلة
rows.claim: They read بعوضة in the nominative; Ibn Jinni explains it as a relative clause with an omitted resumptive pronoun.
rows.anchor: وقرأ الضحاك وإبراهيم بن أبي عبلة ورويت "بعوضة" بالرفع

rows.speaker: سيبويه
rows.claim: His example 'I am not one who says anything to you' illustrates omission of the resumptive pronoun in this construction.
rows.anchor: وحكى سيبويه: ما أنا بالذي قائل لك شيئا

rows.speaker: الكسائي وأبو عبيدة
rows.claim: They read 'what is above it' as anything more contemptible or smaller, as in saying a person is even worse than the description given.
rows.anchor: فما دونها في الصغر، والحقارة، كما إذا وصف رجل باللؤم والشح

rows.speaker: الرازي
rows.claim: He says most critical scholars adopt the interpretation that 'above it' means lower in size or worth.
rows.anchor: وهذا قول الكسائي وأبي عبيدة، قال الرازي: وأكثر المحققين

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: A hadith says that if the world weighed as much as a mosquito's wing with God, He would not give a disbeliever even a drink of water.
rows.anchor: وفي الحديث: "لو أن الدنيا تزن عند الله جناح بعوضة ما سقى كافرا منها شربة ماء"

rows.speaker: قتادة بن دعامة وابن جرير
rows.claim: They take 'above it' to mean something larger, since nothing is more insignificant or smaller than a mosquito; Ibn Jarir chooses this view.
rows.anchor: فما فوقها: فما هو أكبر منها؛ لأنه ليس شيء أحقر ولا أصغر من البعوضة

rows.speaker: عائشة
rows.claim: A Prophetic report says a Muslim is not pricked by a thorn or anything greater without gaining a rank and losing a sin; Ibn Kathir cites it in support of the larger-than-mosquito reading.
rows.anchor: ما من مسلم يشاك شوكة فما فوقها إلا كتبت له بها درجة ومحيت عنه بها خطيئة

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: God does not consider any example too small to use, just as He does not disdain creating small creatures; the Qur'an uses many other parables, including flies, spiders, trees, servants, and partners.
rows.anchor: فأخبر أنه لا يستصغر (3) شيئا يضرب به مثلا ولو كان في الحقارة والصغر

rows.speaker: بعض السلف
rows.claim: A predecessor said that failing to understand a Qur'anic parable should make one weep, since only the learned understand them.
rows.anchor: إذا سمعت المثل في القرآن فلم أفهمه بكيت على نفسي

rows.speaker: مجاهد
rows.claim: Believers affirm Qur'anic parables, small and great, as truth from their Lord, and God guides them by them.
rows.anchor: الأمثال صغيرها وكبيرها يؤمن بها المؤمنون ويعلمون أنها الحق من ربهم

rows.speaker: قتادة
rows.claim: Believers know that the parable is the speech of the Merciful and comes from God; Mujahid, Hasan, and Rabi are reported to say similarly.
rows.anchor: أي: يعلمون أنه كلام الرحمن، وأنه من عند الله

rows.speaker: أبو العالية
rows.claim: He identifies the example here as the parable, and connects the disbelievers' question to the parallel discussion of the number of Hell's keepers in al-Muddaththir.
rows.anchor: يعني: هذا المثل: {وأما الذين كفروا فيقولون ماذا أراد الله بهذا مثلا} كما قال في سورة المدثر

rows.speaker: ابن عباس وابن مسعود وناس من الصحابة
rows.claim: Al-Suddi's report identifies those led astray by the parable as hypocrites and those guided as believers; the former add error by knowingly rejecting a fitting truth, while believers gain guidance and faith by recognizing it.
rows.anchor: {يضل به كثيرا} يعني: المنافقين، {ويهدي به كثيرا} يعني المؤمنين

rows.speaker: أبو العالية
rows.claim: He identifies those misled by the parable as people of hypocrisy; Rabi ibn Anas says the same.
rows.anchor: قال أبو العالية: {وما يضل به إلا الفاسقين} قال: هم أهل النفاق

rows.speaker: ابن عباس
rows.claim: Through Mujahid, Ibn Abbas says disbelievers recognize the truth and then disbelieve in it.
rows.anchor: يقول: يعرفه الكافرون فيكفرون به

rows.speaker: قتادة
rows.claim: They committed disobedience, so God led them further astray on account of their disobedience.
rows.anchor: فسقوا، فأضلهم الله على فسقهم

rows.speaker: سعد بن أبي وقاص
rows.claim: A report through Mus'ab ibn Sa'd says 'He misleads many' refers to the Khawarij.
rows.anchor: عن مصعب بن سعد، عن سعد {يضل به كثيرا} يعني الخوارج

rows.speaker: سعد بن أبي وقاص
rows.claim: In another report, Sa'd identifies those who break God's covenant as the Haruriyya; Ibn Kathir says this is an interpretation if the report is sound, not a claim that the verse specifically predicts the Khawarij.
rows.anchor: فقال: هم الحرورية. وهذا الإسناد إن صح عن سعد بن أبي وقاص، رضي الله عنه، فهو تفسير على المعنى

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: The Haruriyya arose after revelation, but they fall under the verse's description because they left the imam's obedience and Islamic ordinances.
rows.anchor: فإن أولئك لم يكونوا حال نزول الآية، وإنما هم داخلون بوصفهم فيها

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: In Arabic, فسق means leaving obedience; the date leaves its skin and a mouse is called a little fasiq for leaving its hole to cause harm.
rows.anchor: والفاسق في اللغة: هو الخارج عن الطاعة أيضا. وتقول العرب: فسقت الرطبة:

rows.speaker: عائشة
rows.claim: A report in both Ṣaḥīḥ collections permits killing five harmful creatures in the sanctuary and outside it: crow, kite, scorpion, mouse, and vicious dog.
rows.anchor: خمس فواسق يقتلن في الحل والحرم: الغراب، والحدأة، والعقرب، والفأرة

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Fasq includes both unbelief and sin, but the unbeliever's is graver; the intended fasiqun here are unbelievers, as the following traits distinguish them from believers.
rows.anchor: فالفاسق يشمل (1) الكافر والعاصي، ولكن فسق الكافر أشد وأفحش

rows.speaker: بعض المفسرين
rows.claim: One view takes the covenant as God's commands to obey and prohibitions against disobedience, conveyed in scripture and through messengers; breaking it means failing to act on it.
rows.anchor: هو وصية الله إلى خلقه وأمره إياهم بما أمرهم به من طاعته، ونهيه إياهم عما نهاهم عنه من معصيته

rows.speaker: ابن جرير ومقاتل بن حيان
rows.claim: They identify the covenant with the Torah's charge to its People of the Book to follow Muhammad when sent and affirm him; breaking it is knowingly denying him and concealing what they had pledged to disclose.
rows.anchor: وهذا اختيار ابن جرير رحمه الله وقول مقاتل بن حيان

rows.speaker: مقاتل بن حيان
rows.claim: Another view extends the verse to all unbelievers, polytheists, and hypocrites: God gave them rational evidence of His lordship and prophetic miracles, yet they denied the truth of messengers and scriptures.
rows.anchor: بل عنى بهذه الآية جميع أهل الكفر والشرك والنفاق

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Ibn Kathir calls this broad interpretation good; al-Zamakhshari leans toward it, taking the covenant as the rational evidence for God's oneness, like the primordial testimony and the covenant in scripture.
rows.anchor: وهو حسن، [وإليه مال الزمخشري

rows.speaker: مقاتل بن حيان
rows.claim: A further view identifies the covenant as the pledge God took from Adam's descendants; breaking it means failing to fulfill it.
rows.anchor: العهد الذي أخذه عليهم حين أخرجهم من صلب آدم

rows.speaker: أبو العالية
rows.claim: Hypocrites show six traits when they have the upper hand: lying, breaking promises, betraying trusts, breaking God's covenant, severing commanded ties, and spreading corruption; when weak they show only the first three. Rabi ibn Anas agrees.
rows.anchor: قال: هي ست خصال من (3) المنافقين إذا كانت فيهم الظهرة (4) على الناس

rows.speaker: السدي
rows.claim: The covenant was the Qur'an's charge, which people accepted and then broke by disbelieving.
rows.anchor: هو ما عهد إليهم في القرآن فأقروا به ثم كفروا فنقضوه

rows.speaker: قتادة وابن جرير
rows.claim: The severed connection means kinship ties, as in 47:22; Ibn Jarir favors this interpretation.
rows.anchor: قيل: المراد به صلة الأرحام والقرابات، كما فسره قتادة

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: A broader interpretation includes everything God commanded people to connect or do, which they severed or abandoned.
rows.anchor: فكل ما أمر الله بوصله وفعله قطعوه وتركوه

rows.speaker: مقاتل بن حيان
rows.claim: He says these losers lose in the afterlife, as also stated in 13:25.
rows.anchor: قال (8) في الآخرة، وهذا كما قال تعالى: {أولئك لهم اللعنة ولهم سوء الدار}

rows.speaker: ابن عباس
rows.claim: As transmitted by al-Dahhak, loss attributed to non-Muslims means unbelief, while loss attributed to Muslims means sin.
rows.anchor: كل شيء نسبه الله إلى غير أهل الإسلام من اسم مثل خاسر، فإنما يعني به الكفر

rows.speaker: ابن جرير
rows.claim: Losers are those who diminish their own selves and share of God's mercy through disobedience, like a merchant who loses capital; disbelievers and hypocrites are deprived of mercy when most in need of it.
rows.anchor: الخاسرون: جمع خاسر، وهم الناقصون أنفسهم [و] (9) حظوظهم بمعصيتهم الله من رحمته

rows.speaker: جرير بن عطية
rows.claim: Al-Tabari cites Jarir's verse as lexical evidence for خسار, the verbal noun meaning loss.
rows.anchor: إن سليطا في الخسار إنه … أولاد قوم خلقوا أقنه

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: God's command to Abraham to submit meant making worship sincere for Him and yielding in obedience; Abraham answered in both religious law and his created nature.
rows.anchor: أي: أمره الله (1) بالإخلاص له والاستسلام والانقياد، فأجاب إلى ذلك شرعا وقدرا

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: The pronoun in 'he enjoined it' refers either to Abraham's religion of submission to God or to the statement, 'I have submitted to the Lord of the worlds.'
rows.anchor: أي: وصى بهذه الملة (2) وهي الإسلام لله [أو يعود الضمير على الكلمة

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Abraham and Jacob lovingly preserved the religion until death and enjoined it on their descendants, as with the lasting word in 43:28.
rows.anchor: لحرصهم عليها ومحبتهم لها حافظوا عليها إلى حين الوفاة ووصوا أبناءهم بها

rows.speaker: بعض السلف
rows.claim: Some early readers put Yaqub in the accusative, coordinated with Abraham's sons, meaning Abraham also enjoined his grandson Yaqub, who was present.
rows.anchor: وقد قرأ بعض السلف "ويعقوب" بالنصب عطفا على بنيه

rows.speaker: القشيري
rows.claim: Al-Qushayri, as quoted by al-Qurtubi, claims Yaqub was born only after Abraham died; Ibn Kathir says this needs sound evidence and holds that Yaqub was likely born during Abraham and Sarah's lifetime.
rows.anchor: أن يعقوب إنما ولد بعد وفاة إبراهيم، ويحتاج مثل هذا إلى دليل صحيح

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: The wording about the promise of Isaac and, after Isaac, Yaqub implies Yaqub existed in Abraham's lifetime; naming him among Isaac's descendants would otherwise have little point, and 29:27 and 21:72 also say God granted Abraham Yaqub.
rows.anchor: فلو لم يوجد يعقوب في حياتهما لما كان لذكره من بين ذرية إسحاق كبير فائدة

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Ibn Kathir also notes the earlier books' identification of Yaqub as builder of Jerusalem and the Prophetic report that Jerusalem followed the Sacred Mosque by forty years; Ibn Hibban's chronology tying Solomon's rebuilding directly to Abraham is rejected as spanning thousands of years.
rows.anchor: وأيضا فإنه باني بيت المقدس، كما نطقت بذلك الكتب المتقدمة

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: The following account of Jacob's own charge to his children supports reading him here among those who enjoined the faith.
rows.anchor: وأيضا فإن ذكر وصية يعقوب لبنيه سيأتي ذكرها قريبا

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: The command means to live rightly and remain steadfast so God grants death in that state; people generally die and are resurrected in the condition they followed, and God makes good intentions easier to fulfill.
rows.anchor: أحسنوا في حال الحياة والزموا هذا ليرزقكم (5) الله الوفاة عليه

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: This does not contradict the sound hadith about one whose final recorded destiny overtakes deeds near the end, since some versions clarify that the contrary deeds were only what appeared to people; 92:5–10 describes God's facilitation toward outcomes.
rows.anchor: "فيعمل بعمل أهل الجنة فيما يبدو للناس، ويعمل بعمل أهل النار فيما يبدو للناس.

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Jacob's deathbed instruction argues against Arab polytheists descended from Ismail and Israelite disbelievers: he charged his sons to worship God alone; Ismail is included as their father by rhetorical predominance although he was their uncle.
rows.anchor: وهذا من باب التغليب لأن إسماعيل عمه

rows.speaker: النحاس
rows.claim: Al-Nahhas says Arabs call an uncle a father; al-Qurtubi transmits the point.
rows.anchor: قال النحاس: والعرب تسمي العم أبا، نقله القرطبي

rows.speaker: أبو بكر
rows.claim: Some use this verse to support the grandfather as a father who blocks siblings from inheritance; al-Bukhari transmits this as Abu Bakr's view through Ibn Abbas and Ibn al-Zubayr, without disagreement reported from him.
rows.anchor: وقد استدل بهذه الآية من جعل الجد أبا وحجب به الإخوة، كما هو قول الصديق

rows.speaker: عائشة والحسن البصري وطاوس وعطاء وأبو حنيفة
rows.claim: They, along with many early and later scholars, hold that the grandfather takes the position of a father and excludes siblings.
rows.anchor: وإليه ذهبت عائشة أم المؤمنين، وبه يقول الحسن البصري وطاوس وعطاء

rows.speaker: مالك والشافعي وأحمد
rows.claim: Malik, al-Shafi'i, and Ahmad according to his well-known position hold that the grandfather shares inheritance with siblings; Malik attributes this view to several Companions and others.
rows.anchor: وقال مالك والشافعي وأحمد في المشهور عنه أنه يقاسم الإخوة

rows.speaker: أبو يوسف ومحمد بن الحسن
rows.claim: Abu Hanifa's two companions, Abu Yusuf and Muhammad ibn al-Hasan, chose the view that the grandfather excludes siblings; Ibn Kathir says fuller evidence is discussed elsewhere.
rows.anchor: واختاره صاحبا أبي حنيفة القاضي: أبو يوسف، ومحمد بن الحسن

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: 'One God' means that they affirm His sole divinity and associate nothing with Him; 'submitted' means obedient and humble. Islam is the religion of every prophet despite differing laws and paths, as in 3:83 and 21:25 and the hadith that the prophets share one religion.
rows.anchor: أي: نوحده بالألوهية، ولا نشرك به شيئا غيره {ونحن له مسلمون} أي: مطيعون خاضعون

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: The earlier community has passed: descent from prophets and righteous forebears does not benefit descendants without their own good deeds; each is accountable for what they themselves did.
rows.anchor: إن السلف الماضين من آبائكم من الأنبياء والصالحين لا ينفعكم انتسابكم إليهم

rows.speaker: أبو العالية والربيع وقتادة
rows.claim: They identify the departed community as Abraham, Ismail, Isaac, Jacob, and the tribes; an accompanying report says that one slowed by his deeds is not hastened by his lineage.
rows.anchor: يعني: إبراهيم، وإسماعيل، وإسحاق، ويعقوب، والأسباط

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Because the concealers knowingly hid revelation, God is angry with them; He will neither look favorably at nor praise them, but will punish them painfully.
rows.anchor: وذلك لأنه غضبان عليهم، لأنهم كتموا وقد علموا، فاستحقوا الغضب، فلا ينظر إليهم ولا يزكيهم

rows.speaker: أبو هريرة
rows.claim: A Prophetic report in Muslim lists three whom God will not speak to, look at, or purify: an old adulterer, a lying king, and an arrogant poor man.
rows.anchor: شيخ زان، وملك كذاب، وعائل مستكبر

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: They traded away guidance by abandoning scripture's descriptions and good tidings of Muhammad, his mission, and the duty to follow and affirm him; they chose denial and concealment instead, and exchanged forgiveness for punishment and its causes.
rows.anchor: أي: اعتاضوا عن الهدى، وهو نشر ما في كتبهم من صفة الرسول

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: The question 'How patient they are with the Fire!' marvels at their endurance of terrible punishment, torment, and shackles, while asking God for protection from it.
rows.anchor: يتعجب من رآهم فيها من صبرهم على ذلك، مع (6) شدة ما هم فيه من العذاب

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: An alternative interpretation is 'How persistent they are in deeds of disobedience that lead them to the Fire.'
rows.anchor: ما أدومهم لعمل المعاصي التي تفضي بهم إلى النار

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Their punishment follows because God sent scripture to Muhammad and earlier prophets to establish truth and refute falsehood, while these people mocked the signs, disobeyed scripture's command to disclose knowledge, denied the final Messenger, and concealed his description.
rows.anchor: كتابهم يأمرهم بإظهار العلم ونشره، فخالفوه وكذبوه

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: A small believing force faced Goliath's larger army and asked God to pour patience upon them, steady them against fleeing or failing, and grant victory over the unbelievers.
rows.anchor: لما واجه حزب الإيمان -وهم قليل-من أصحاب طالوت لعدوهم أصحاب جالوت -وهم عدد كثير-

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Isra'ili reports say David killed Goliath with a sling; Talut had promised him his daughter, a share of his wealth, and a role in government, and kept the promise before kingship eventually passed to David along with prophethood.
rows.anchor: ذكروا في الإسرائيليات: أنه قتله بمقلاع كان في يده

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: God gave David Talut's kingdom and wisdom, meaning prophethood after Samuel, and taught him knowledge God chose for him.
rows.anchor: {والحكمة} أي: النبوة بعد شمويل {وعلمه مما يشاء} أي: مما يشاء الله

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: God prevents some people from harming others; without Talut's fighting and David's courage, Israel would have perished. The same principle appears in 22:40.
rows.anchor: أي: لولاه يدفع عن قوم بآخرين، كما دفع عن بني إسرائيل بمقاتلة طالوت

rows.speaker: ابن عمر
rows.claim: A Prophetic report says God wards off affliction from a hundred neighboring households through a righteous Muslim; Ibn Kathir grades its chain weak because Yahya ibn Sa'id al-'Attar is very weak.
rows.anchor: إن الله ليدفع بالمسلم الصالح عن مائة أهل بيت من جيرانه البلاء

rows.speaker: جابر بن عبد الله
rows.claim: A report says God rectifies a righteous Muslim's children, grandchildren, and neighborhood and protects them while such a person remains among them; Ibn Kathir calls it strange and weak.
rows.anchor: وهذا أيضا غريب ضعيف لما تقدم أيضا

rows.speaker: ثوبان
rows.claim: A raised report says seven people remain in the community through whom victory, rain, and provision come until God's command arrives.
rows.anchor: لا يزال فيكم سبعة بهم تنصرون وبهم تمطرون وبهم ترزقون

rows.speaker: عبادة بن الصامت
rows.claim: A report says thirty 'substitutes' uphold the earth and bring rain and victory; Qatada hopes Hasan is among them.
rows.anchor: الأبدال في أمتي ثلاثون بهم تقوم الأرض، وبهم تمطرون وبهم تنصرون

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: This is the longest verse in the Qur'an; Ibn Shihab says he was told it was the latest Qur'anic verse revealed at the Throne.
rows.anchor: أطول آية في القرآن العظيم

rows.speaker: ابن عباس
rows.claim: A Prophetic report says Adam first denied an agreement: God showed him his descendants, including David, gave David forty years from Adam's thousand-year lifespan, and documented and witnessed the gift; Adam later denied it until shown the record. A version says David lived one hundred and Adam completed one thousand. Ibn Kathir calls the report very strange and notes weakness in Ali ibn Zayd's narrations, though al-Hakim gives variants through Abu Hurayra.
rows.anchor: إن أول من جحد آدم، عليه السلام، أن الله لما خلق آدم، مسح ظهره

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Writing deferred transactions is guidance that better preserves the amount and due date and keeps the testimony accurate, as the verse's stated rationale explains.
rows.anchor: أن يكتبوها، ليكون ذلك أحفظ لمقدارها وميقاتها، وأضبط للشاهد فيها

rows.speaker: ابن عباس
rows.claim: Through Mujahid, Ibn Abbas says the verse was revealed concerning salam, an advance payment due at a known term.
rows.anchor: أنزلت في السلم إلى أجل معلوم

rows.speaker: ابن عباس
rows.claim: Ibn Abbas swears that deferred forward sale for a specified term is permitted by God and reads this verse as evidence; al-Bukhari transmits it.
rows.anchor: أشهد أن السلف المضمون إلى أجل مسمى أن الله أحله وأذن فيه

rows.speaker: ابن عباس
rows.claim: When people in Medina paid in advance for fruit deliveries two or three years ahead, the Prophet instructed that advance sales specify a known measure, weight, and term; the report is in both Ṣaḥīḥ collections.
rows.anchor: من أسلف فليسلف في كيل معلوم، ووزن معلوم، إلى أجل معلوم

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Writing is ordered for documentation and preservation, not because religion itself requires writing: Qur'an and Sunna are made easy to memorize. Specific transactions should be written as guidance, not obligation, according to one view, reconciling the instruction with the report that the community neither writes nor calculates.
rows.anchor: فأمروا أمر إرشاد لا أمر إيجاب، كما ذهب إليه بعضهم

rows.speaker: ابن جريج
rows.claim: He says a borrower should write down a debt and a buyer should have witnesses.
rows.anchor: قال ابن جريج: من ادان فليكتب، ومن ابتاع فليشهد

rows.speaker: قتادة
rows.claim: He recounts Abu Sulayman al-Mar'ashi's warning: a seller who grants credit without writing or witnesses and is later cheated has wronged himself by disobeying God, so his plea is not answered.
rows.anchor: رجل باع بيعا إلى أجل فلم يشهد ولم يكتب، فلما حل ماله جحده صاحبه

rows.speaker: أبو سعيد والشعبي والربيع بن أنس والحسن وابن جريج وابن زيد
rows.claim: They hold that writing transactions was initially obligatory, then abrogated by the option to trust one another and discharge the entrusted obligation in 2:283.
rows.anchor: كان ذلك واجبا ثم نسخ بقوله: {فإن أمن بعضكم بعضا فليؤد الذي اؤتمن أمانته}

rows.speaker: أبو هريرة
rows.claim: A Prophetic story tells of an Israelite borrower who could find no ship to repay a thousand dinars, placed the money and a note in a sealed log, and entrusted it to the sea after invoking God as witness and guarantor; the lender found it, and the borrower later came with repayment too.
rows.anchor: فأخذ خشبة فنقرها فأدخل فيها ألف دينار وصحيفة معها إلى صاحبها

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Ibn Kathir calls the preceding loan story's chain sound and says al-Bukhari narrated it in seven sound routes, sometimes through 'Abd Allah ibn Salih from al-Layth.
rows.anchor: وهذا إسناد صحيح (4) وقد رواه البخاري في سبعة مواضع من طرق صحيحة (5)

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: A writer must record fairly and justly, without bias or adding to or reducing the agreed terms.
rows.anchor: ولا يكتب إلا ما اتفقوا عليه من غير زيادة ولا نقصان

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Someone who knows how to write should not refuse a request; writing for those unable to do so is charity, as supported by reports about helping a worker and concealing knowledge.
rows.anchor: فكما علمه الله ما لم يكن يعلم، فليتصدق على غيره ممن لا يحسن الكتابة

rows.speaker: مجاهد وعطاء
rows.claim: They hold that it is obligatory for a capable writer to write.
rows.anchor: وقال مجاهد وعطاء: واجب على الكاتب أن يكتب

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: The debtor dictates the debt and must fear God, withholding none of it; if the debtor is wasteful and legally restricted, young, insane, or unable to dictate through speech difficulty or ignorance, the guardian dictates fairly.
rows.anchor: أي: وليملل المدين على الكاتب ما في ذمته من الدين، وليتق الله في ذلك

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Witnesses accompany writing for additional assurance. In financial matters, one man and two women may testify; Ibn Kathir connects this arrangement to a hadith describing women's testimony as half a man's and explaining their lesser reason and religious practice.
rows.anchor: وهذا إنما يكون في الأموال وما يقصد به المال

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: The condition that witnesses be approved implies their probity; al-Shafi'i uses it to specify other unqualified Qur'anic witness commands, and some use it to reject unknown-status witnesses.
rows.anchor: فيه دلالة على اشتراط العدالة في الشهود

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: If one woman forgets, the other reminds her; another reading intensifies the verb. Ibn Kathir rejects the claim that having two women together makes them equivalent to a man and prefers the reminder interpretation.
rows.anchor: أي: يحصل لها ذكرى بما وقع به الإشهاد، ولهذا قرأ آخرون: "فتذكر" بالتشديد

rows.speaker: قتادة والربيع بن أنس
rows.claim: They interpret 'when called' as a summons to undertake testimony, which witnesses must accept; this makes taking testimony a communal obligation.
rows.anchor: إذا دعوا للتحمل فعليهم الإجابة

rows.speaker: الجمهور
rows.claim: The majority interprets the summons as one to give testimony already borne; a witness must answer when personally required, otherwise the duty is communal.
rows.anchor: المراد بقوله: {ولا يأب الشهداء إذا ما دعوا} للأداء، لحقيقة قوله: {الشهداء}

rows.speaker: مجاهد وأبو مجلز
rows.claim: If invited to take testimony, one may choose; after having witnessed, one must respond when called to testify.
rows.anchor: إذا دعيت لتشهد فأنت بالخيار، وإذا شهدت فدعيت (4) فأجب

rows.speaker: زيد بن خالد
rows.claim: A Prophetic report calls the best witnesses those who bring their testimony before being asked for it.
rows.anchor: ألا أخبركم بخير الشهداء؟ الذي يأتي بشهادته قبل أن يسألها

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Other reports condemn witnesses who testify before being asked, whose oaths and testimony precede each other, or who testify without a request; these are false witnesses.
rows.anchor: فهؤلاء شهود الزور

rows.speaker: ابن عباس والحسن البصري
rows.claim: They say the prohibition covers both taking testimony and giving it.
rows.anchor: أنها تعم الحالين: التحمل والأداء

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Do not grow weary of recording a debt, large or small, through its due date; writing deferred claims is more just before God, strengthens testimony by helping witnesses remember, and reduces doubt in disputes.
rows.anchor: أي: هذا الذي أمرناكم به من الكتابة للحق إذا كان مؤجلا هو {أقسط عند الله}

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: An immediate cash trade may go unwritten because no harm results from omitting a record.
rows.anchor: أي: إذا كان البيع بالحاضر يدا بيد، فلا بأس بعدم الكتابة

rows.speaker: سعيد بن جبير
rows.claim: He says buyers should witness their rights whether or not a term is involved; similar views are reported from Jabir ibn Zayd, Mujahid, Ata, and al-Dahhak.
rows.anchor: أشهدوا على حقكم إذا كان فيه أجل أو لم يكن

rows.speaker: الشعبي والحسن
rows.claim: They say the command to witness sales was abrogated by the option to trust one another and return the entrusted property in 2:283.
rows.anchor: هذا الأمر منسوخ بقوله: {فإن أمن بعضكم بعضا فليؤد الذي اؤتمن أمانته}

rows.speaker: الجمهور
rows.claim: The majority treats witnessing sales as guidance and recommendation, not obligation; the report of the Prophet's disputed horse purchase and Khuzaima's extraordinary testimony supports this.
rows.anchor: وهذا الأمر محمول عند الجمهور على الإرشاد والندب، لا على الوجوب

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Abu Dawud and al-Nasa'i transmit the horse-purchase story through other routes from al-Zuhri, supporting the report about Khuzaima's testimony.
rows.anchor: وهكذا رواه أبو داود من حديث شعيب، والنسائي من رواية محمد بن الوليد الزبيري

rows.speaker: أبو موسى
rows.claim: A report says prayers are not answered for three: a man who keeps a badly behaved wife without divorcing her, a guardian who gives an orphan's wealth before maturity, and a lender who lends without witnesses. Al-Hakim calls its chain sound by the two Ṣaḥīḥ collections' criteria, but notes Shu'ba's companions stop it at Abu Musa and agree on a different report through that chain.
rows.anchor: ثلاثة يدعون الله فلا يستجاب لهم: رجل له امرأة سيئة الخلق فلم يطلقها

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Ibn Kathir says witnessing remains the prudent safeguard.
rows.anchor: ولكن الاحتياط هو الإشهاد

rows.speaker: الحسن وقتادة
rows.claim: They understand the prohibition as forbidding a writer from recording anything contrary to what was dictated or a witness from falsely testifying or concealing testimony.
rows.anchor: فيكتب هذا خلاف ما يملى، ويشهد هذا بخلاف ما سمع أو يكتمها بالكلية

rows.speaker: ابن عباس
rows.claim: Another interpretation forbids burdening or harming the writer and witness: a person summons them, and they explain that they are occupied, but he insists that they were commanded to answer; Ibn Abbas says the caller may not harm them. Similar views are attributed to many early authorities.
rows.anchor: قال: يأتي الرجل فيدعوهما إلى الكتاب والشهادة، فيقولان: إنا على حاجة

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Disobeying these directions and doing what was forbidden is an abiding sin from which people cannot escape.
rows.anchor: أي: إن خالفتم ما أمرتم به، وفعلتم ما نهيتم عنه، فإنه فسق كائن بكم، أي: لازم لكم

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Fearing God means keeping watch, following His commands, and leaving His prohibitions; the promise that God teaches those who fear Him is compared with the discernment of 8:29 and light from 57:28.
rows.anchor: أي: خافوه وراقبوه، واتبعوا أمره واتركوا زجره

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: God knows the realities, interests, and consequences of all things; nothing is hidden from His knowledge, which encompasses all beings.
rows.anchor: أي: هو عالم بحقائق الأمور ومصالحها وعواقبها، فلا يخفى عليه شيء من الأشياء

rows.speaker: ابن عباس
rows.claim: If travelers cannot find a scribe, or even paper, ink, or pen, they should take a pledge in the creditor's possession in place of writing.
rows.anchor: أو وجدوه ولم يجد قرطاسا أو دواة أو قلما فرهن مقبوضة

rows.speaker: الشافعي والجمهور
rows.claim: They infer from 'pledges taken' that a pledge is not binding until it is taken into possession.
rows.anchor: على أن الرهن لا يلزم إلا بالقبض، كما هو مذهب الشافعي والجمهور

rows.speaker: رواية عن أحمد وطائفة
rows.claim: They infer that the pledge must be held by the creditor, the pledgee.
rows.anchor: على أنه لا بد أن يكون الرهن مقبوضا في يد المرتهن

rows.speaker: مجاهد وغيرهم من السلف
rows.claim: Some early authorities infer from the verse that pledges are lawful only while traveling.
rows.anchor: على أنه لا يكون الرهن مشروعا إلا في السفر، قاله مجاهد وغيره

rows.speaker: أنس
rows.claim: A report in both Ṣaḥīḥ collections says the Prophet died with his armor pledged to a Jew for thirty wasqs of barley as food for his family; variants identify the Jew as from Medina or Abu al-Shahm.
rows.anchor: توفي ودرعه مرهونة عند يهودي على ثلاثين وسقا من شعير

rows.speaker: أبو سعيد الخدري
rows.claim: He says the permission to trust one another superseded the preceding direction; Ibn Abi Hatim gives the report with a good chain.
rows.anchor: هذه نسخت ما قبلها

rows.speaker: الشعبي
rows.claim: When parties trust one another, they may omit writing or witnesses.
rows.anchor: وقال الشعبي: إذا ائتمن بعضكم (1) بعضا فلا بأس ألا تكتبوا أو لا تشهدوا

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: The person trusted to repay or return property is the one commanded to fulfill the trust; a report from Samura says the hand is responsible for what it takes until it returns it.
rows.anchor: يعنى: المؤتمن، كما جاء في الحديث الذي رواه الإمام أحمد وأهل السنن

rows.speaker: ابن عباس
rows.claim: Concealing testimony means hiding, suppressing, or withholding it; Ibn Abbas and others treat false testimony and withholding testimony as major sins.
rows.anchor: لا تخفوها وتغلوها ولا تظهروها

rows.speaker: السدي
rows.claim: He explains that the heart of someone who conceals testimony is wicked; Ibn Kathir links this to 5:106 and the command in 4:135 to uphold justice.
rows.anchor: قال السدي: يعني: فاجر قلبه

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Some People of the Book truly believe in God, the Qur'an, and their own earlier scriptures, submit humbly, and refuse to conceal Muhammad's description and glad tidings for a small gain. They are the finest of the Jews and Christians: only a few Jews, such as Abdullah ibn Salam, and many Christians are so inclined.
rows.anchor: وهؤلاء هم خيرة أهل الكتاب وصفوتهم، سواء كانوا هودا أو نصارى

rows.speaker: جعفر بن أبي طالب
rows.claim: When Ja'far recited Surah Maryam before the Negus and his bishops and priests, they wept with him until their beards were wet.
rows.anchor: لما قرأ سورة {كهيعص} بحضرة النجاشي ملك الحبشة، وعنده البطاركة والقساوسة (1) بكى وبكوا معه

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: In both Ṣaḥīḥ collections, the Prophet announced the Negus's death to his companions, called him their brother in Abyssinia, and led them in funeral prayer outdoors.
rows.anchor: "إن أخا (4) لكم بالحبشة قد مات فصلوا عليه"

rows.speaker: أنس بن مالك
rows.claim: One occasion report says that after the Prophet called the dead Negus a brother and asked people to seek forgiveness for him, objectors called him a foreign pagan in Abyssinia; the verse followed. Other routes give the report from Hasan as a mursal narration and via Humayd from Anas.
rows.anchor: استغفروا لأخيكم. فقال بعض الناس: يأمرنا أن نستغفر لعلج مات بأرض الحبشة

rows.speaker: جابر
rows.claim: A report says the Prophet identified the deceased as As'hama, performed an absentee funeral prayer with four takbirs, and hypocrites objected to praying for a foreign pagan; the verse was revealed. Ibn Kathir cites its route through Abu Bakr al-Hudhali from Qatada and Sa'id ibn al-Musayyib.
rows.anchor: حين مات النجاشي: "إن أخاكم أصحمة قد مات". فخرج رسول الله صلى الله عليه وسلم فصلى كما يصلي

rows.speaker: عبد الله بن الزبير
rows.claim: A report says refugees offered to fight enemies who had attacked the Negus to repay his protection, but he answered that aid from God was better than aid from people; al-Hakim calls its chain sound though it is not in the two Ṣaḥīḥ collections.
rows.anchor: لا دواء بنصرة الله عز وجل خير من دواء بنصرة الناس

rows.speaker: عائشة
rows.claim: A report recorded by Abu Dawud says that when the Negus died, people used to say that a light could still be seen over his grave.
rows.anchor: لما مات النجاشي كنا نحدث أنه لا يزال يرى على (2) قبره نور (3)

rows.speaker: مجاهد
rows.claim: He explains 'among the People of the Book' as those People of the Book who became Muslims.
rows.anchor: وقال ابن أبي نجيح، عن مجاهد: {وإن من أهل الكتاب} يعني: مسلمة أهل الكتاب

rows.speaker: الحسن البصري
rows.claim: He identifies the believers as earlier People of the Book who recognized Islam and followed Muhammad; they receive two rewards, for their prior faith and for following him.
rows.anchor: قال: هم أهل الكتاب الذين كانوا قبل محمد صلى الله عليه وسلم، فاتبعوه وعرفوا الإسلام

rows.speaker: أبو موسى
rows.claim: A Prophetic report in both Ṣaḥīḥ collections says three receive a double reward, including a person from the People of the Book who believed in his prophet and then believed in Muhammad.
rows.anchor: ورجل من أهل الكتاب آمن بنبيه وآمن بي
